subject: MAP sync: privacy & deployment — VPC vs on-prem tradeoffs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint: proposed decisions on data handling & deployment mode

Hi Alice & Tom —

Quick sync note following Friday’s demo. We captured the MAP items that are blocking your procurement/legal review and wanted to propose concrete decisions so we can close the pilot milestones next week. Below are the proposals (please treat as a record we can edit):

1) Deployment mode
   - Proposal A (preferred): VPC-hosted Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC peering to avoid on-prem hardware procurement.
   - Proposal B (fallback): On-prem packaged deployment for restricted workloads that cannot leave air-gapped environments.
   - Recommendation: Start with Proposal A for the pilot (scope: inference for non-PII endpoints) and scope a small on-prem POC for PII-sensitive flows if needed.

2) Data handling & retention
   - Inference logs: 30 days by default (configurable).
   - Model input KV cache: ephemeral by default (0 retention); option to enable 7/30/90 day caching for performance with explicit opt-in.
   - PII: Redwood will run customer-supplied redaction rules in the ingestion layer for any endpoint flagged as containing PII; we also recommend client-side redaction for highest assurance.

3) Key management & audit
   - Integrate with Acme KMS (AES-256 + HSM where available). Key rotations: quarterly recommended.
   - Audit logs: we can export to your Splunk/CloudWatch with 90-day retention for the pilot; longer windows available via enterprise add-on.

Action items (owners & timeline):
  - Alice / Acme Legal: confirm whether inference logs or input data are classified as regulated (response by Wed 2026-06-09)
  - Karthik (Redwood): draft VPC peering checklist + firewall rules (due Tue 2026-06-08)
  - Neha (Redwood): prepare a short on-prem POC runbook and cost estimate (due Thu 2026-06-10)
  - Vanessa (Redwood): update MAP spreadsheet with agreed retention values and attach security artifacts (today)

Attachments: MAP_Data_Decision_Log_2026-06-07.xlsx (decision table), Acme_Security_Questionnaire_filled.pdf (answers)

Next steps: brief call Wednesday 6/9 at 11am PT to confirm legal classification and finalize the pilot scope. If Acme confirms non-regulated classification for the initial endpoints we’ll proceed with VPC-hosted pilot and ship Karthik’s peering checklist.

Thanks —
Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa. Short answers below — appreciate the clear options.

• Deployment: Acme is OK to start with VPC-hosted Redwood Private for the pilot (non-PII flows). We’ll need an on-prem option scoped for later.
• Retention: 30 days for inference logs is acceptable for pilot. We will need a 24-hour bleeding-edge redaction requirement for any endpoint that touches customer-identifiable data.
• KMS & audit: we will supply a read-only KMS service principal; legal will follow up on rotation cadence.

Action from our side: I’ll confirm classification for the endpoints by EOD Wednesday (2026-06-09). If anything changes, we’ll surface it immediately.

Quick clarification: for the KV cache, is the 0 default strictly ephemeral or persisted in encrypted local disk for fast restarts? We need assurance that persisted caches are encrypted at rest and that retention can be set to 0.

Cheers,

Hi all — answering Alice’s cache question and noting technical owner items.

KV cache behavior:
 - Default: in-memory ephemeral (restarts clear cache). We only persist to disk when customers enable the performance cache option.
 - Persisted cache: encrypted at rest (AES-256) and stored in the customer-controlled VPC subnet; retention policy is configurable (0/7/30/90).
 - For the pilot we’ll leave persisted cache off unless Acme requests it explicitly.

VPC peering checklist (draft items I’ll deliver Tue):
 - Required CIDR ranges and subnets
 - Firewall rules: outbound-only to Redwood control plane endpoints, explicit allowed ports
 - Route tables for peered endpoints
 - KMS principal binding steps
 - Monitoring endpoint (SN/alerting hook)

On-prem POC runbook (Neha is drafting cost/time estimates) — I suggest we reserve 2 nodes for a minimal inference cluster for performance parity testing and to verify air-gapped installation procedures.

I’ll attach the peering checklist and sample firewall snippet in a follow-up here.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
